cover — The post header — title block with optional eyebrow, subtitle and image.

::cover{eyebrow="Engineering" subtitle="What a markdown twin actually saves" image="/media/cover.png" alt="Token counts side by side"}
tldr — The 1–3 sentence summary an agent or skimmer reads first.

:::tldr Serving a markdown twin cuts what an agent parses by 92 %. `llms.txt` may do nothing. :::
callout — A boxed aside that must not be skipped — a warning, a tip, a note, or a line you want quoted.

:::callout{kind="warning" title="The caveat"} `llms.txt` is the most-recommended and least-evidenced item on the list. :::
pullquote — A sentence lifted from the text (or a cited source) and set large.

:::pullquote{cite="Google Search Central" href="https://developers.google.com/search"} There is no ranking benefit from llms.txt. :::
stat-row — Two to four stats side by side, the numbers a post stands on.

:::stat-row ::stat{value="92%" label="fewer tokens" source="https://snypd.rocks/bench"} ::stat{value="0" label="Google support for llms.txt" source="https://developers.google.com/search"} :::
stat — One number with its label and where it came from.

::stat{value="92%" label="fewer tokens" source="https://snypd.rocks/bench"}
chart — A small static chart rendered to inline SVG at build time from inline data or a YAML file.

:::chart{type="bar" source="https://snypd.rocks/bench" caption="Tokens per page, HTML vs markdown twin" unit="tokens"} - { label: HTML, value: 6120 } - { label: Markdown twin, value: 504 } :::
diagram — A box-and-arrow diagram laid out automatically (layered, deterministic) and rendered to inline SVG at build time.

:::diagram{direction="lr" caption="Content flows from git to two outputs."} nodes: - { id: md, label: markdown + YAML } - { id: build, label: snypd build } - { id: html, label: HTML } - { id: twin, label: .md twin } edges: - { from: md, to: build } - { from: build, to: html } - { from: build, to: twin } :::
flow — An ordered procedure with branches — steps plus yes/no decisions — written as YAML and rendered as a diagram.

:::flow{caption="Publishing lands one item on main; the agent never checks main out."} steps: - Draft on snypd/drafts - Run lint - ask: Lint clean? yes: Open preview no: { then: fix } - id: fix do: Fix the reported rule and re-lint - Human approves - Land that one item on main :::
steps — An ordered procedure, emitted as HowTo schema.

:::steps{title="Add a markdown twin" time="5 min"} 1. **Build** — `snypd build` writes `index.md` beside every `index.html`. 2. **Serve** — answer `Accept: text/markdown` with the twin. 3. **Verify** — `curl -H 'Accept: text/markdown' https://example.com/post/`. :::
faq — Question-and-answer pairs, emitted as FAQPage schema.

:::faq ### Does llms.txt help ranking? No. No search engine has announced support. ### What does help? A markdown twin served on `Accept: text/markdown`. :::
figure — An image with mandatory alt text and an optional caption; the only way to place an image.

::figure{src="/media/twin.png" alt="Side-by-side HTML and markdown of the same post" caption="The `.md` twin is the source file." width="wide"}
cta — One call to action — a title, a line of body and a single button.

::cta{title="Run the bench yourself" body="One binary, one command." button="Install" href="https://snypd.rocks/install"}
